claims.statement: Tom Allen and Tom Kelly, at the Post-Dispatch's request, watched Jim Corbett at a Havlin's Theater matinee and declared him fit to fight.
claims.excerpt: have looked Jim Corbett over carefully, and declare him fit

claims.statement: Tom Allen runs a saloon on Market Street between Sixth and Seventh streets, and also a concert hall over which he presides every night.
claims.excerpt:
They both are running prosperous saloons
on Market street, between Sixth and Seventh streets, Allen having in addition a concert
hall
places: Market Street between Sixth and Seventh, St. Louis

claims.statement: Tom Allen lost money in the Corbett-Sullivan fight because he had misjudged Corbett, thinking him too light and spare.
claims.excerpt:
I lost money on him in the Sullivan fight,
because I misjudged him, th.nking him

quotes.text: He is the fastest and quickest big man I ever saw in my life, bar none.

notes: The condition verdicts on Corbett are opinions, not facts about Allen, so they are left out. The 145-pound claim and the Sullivan betting line are garbled in places in the OCR.
